business_summary: Alphabet is the holding company for Google. It makes money in three ways. (1) Google Services (Q2 2026 revenue $94.540B, +15% YoY) is the profit engine: Search & other $63.271B, YouTube ads $11.055B, and subscriptions/platforms/devices (YouTube Premium, Google One, Play store, Pixel) $12.911B. Advertisers pay Google to put ads next to search results and videos; roughly a quarter of the world's web traffic starts at a Google property. (2) Google Cloud (Q2 2026 revenue $24.768B, +82% YoY) rents computing power, databases, and AI models (Gemini, TPUs) to businesses. (3) Other Bets (Waymo self-driving, Verily and others) is tiny revenue ($0.382B) and loses money (-$1.799B operating loss in Q2 2026). Total Q2 2026 revenue was $119.796B, +24% YoY, with operating income of $40.770B (34% operating margin). Reported Q2 net income of $112.193B and diluted EPS of $9.11 are NOT representative of the operating business: $97.983B of 'other income' was almost entirely unrealized paper gains on private equity stakes (mainly Anthropic and SpaceX). Alphabet should still be winning in 5-10 years because search advertising remains the highest-intent advertising surface ever built, Android/Chrome/Maps/YouTube each have over a billion users feeding a data and distribution flywheel, and Alphabet is one of only a handful of firms that owns the full AI stack (its own chips, data centres, models, and distribution). The open question is not demand; it is how much capital that AI position now costs to defend - 2026 capex guidance was raised to $195-205B, versus $91.4B actually spent in FY2025.

moat.type: Network effects and a data flywheel in Search and YouTube, default-distribution scale via Android/Chrome, enormous scale economies in data centres and custom TPU silicon, and a globally recognised brand

quality.revenue_growth_3y: 12.5% CAGR FY2022->FY2025 ($282.836B -> $402.836B); accelerating, TTM revenue to 2026-06-30 was $445.866B and Q2 2026 grew 24% YoY

quality.roic: ~32% FY2025 (NOPAT $107.4B = operating income $129.039B x (1 - 16.8% effective tax rate), on invested capital ~$335.0B = equity $415.265B + long-term debt $46.547B - cash & marketable securities $126.843B). Declining from ~39% in FY2024 as the AI capex base builds; not yet meaningfully depressed but this is the number to watch.
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: net cash (about -0.8x): cash & marketable securities $242.474B versus total debt $98.165B at 2026-06-30, a net cash position of ~$144.3B, against TTM EBITDA of roughly $173B (TTM operating income $147.628B plus ~$25B depreciation)
quality.fcf_positive: yes but sharply deteriorating: TTM FCF to 2026-06-30 was $53.273B (down from $73.266B in FY2025); Q2 2026 alone was FCF-NEGATIVE at -$5.855B as quarterly capex hit $44.9B

valuation.method: pe only: 24x / 30x / 36x applied to normalized EPS of $9.89. Normalized EPS = TTM operating income $147.628B x (1 - 17.5% tax) / 12,309M diluted shares. We deliberately use operating income, NOT reported EPS, because reported TTM EPS (~$19.90) is inflated by ~$135.7B of unrealized paper gains on private Anthropic/SpaceX stakes that produce no cash. The fcf_yield method was run but excluded from the headline band: TTM FCF/share of $4.33 at 3.5/3.0/2.5% target yields gives $124/$144/$173, which would only be the right answer if the entire $132.4B TTM capex were maintenance spending - it is not (FY2022 capex was $31.5B). Treat $124-173 as the downside anchor if the AI buildout earns nothing. The band also gives NO explicit credit for ~$21.8/share of net cash plus non-marketable equity stakes ($124.259B at 2026-06-30), which is a conservative choice.

bull_case: Wide, durable moat: Search is still the highest-intent advertising surface ever built, and Q2 2026 Search & other revenue grew 17% to $63.271B - the AI-disruption-of-search fear has not shown up in the numbers yet.

Google Cloud is now a genuine second engine: Q2 2026 revenue $24.768B, +82% YoY, with segment operating income of $8.814B versus $13.1B for all of FY2025 - it has flipped from a cash drain to a fast-growing profit contributor.

Full-stack AI ownership is rare: Alphabet designs its own TPUs, builds its own data centres, trains its own Gemini models, and distributes them through Search, Android, Chrome, Workspace and Cloud. Very few competitors control every layer.
Fortress balance sheet: ~$144.3B net cash at 2026-06-30, so the AI capex program can be self-funded without threatening solvency.

Hidden asset value: non-marketable equity securities carried at $124.259B at 2026-06-30 (Anthropic, SpaceX and others), roughly $10/share of carrying value not reflected in our earnings-based fair value band.
Excellent underlying economics: ~60% gross margin, 33% TTM operating margin, ~32% FY2025 ROIC.
risks: Capex shock is the dominant risk. 2026 capex guidance was raised to $195-205B (from $180-190B), versus $91.4B actually spent in FY2025. Q2 2026 free cash flow was negative (-$5.855B). If demand does not materialise, Alphabet will have bought a mountain of depreciating silicon and concrete.
Depreciation drag: today's capex becomes tomorrow's expense. Depreciation was $21.136B in FY2025 and already $13.586B in H1 2026 alone. Operating margins can compress even if revenue holds.

No margin of safety at $325.31 - the price is ~10% ABOVE our base fair value of $296.70, and far above the FCF-based downside anchor of $124-173. We would be paying full price for a successful AI outcome.

Earnings quality: reported net income is currently dominated by unrealized, non-cash marks on private stakes ($97.983B of the $112.193B Q2 net income). These marks can reverse violently and tell us nothing about the operating business.
AI could still disrupt search economics. Chatbot answers may reduce the number of monetisable queries or lower cost-per-click even if Google wins the technology.

Regulation: Alphabet faces ongoing antitrust actions in the US (search distribution and ad tech) and the EU. Remedies could restrict default-search payments or force divestiture of parts of the ad-tech stack.
Advertising is cyclical. A recession hits ad budgets fast, and ~79% of Q2 2026 revenue is still Google Services.

Dual-class share structure means founders retain voting control; outside shareholders have limited ability to influence capital allocation - which matters a great deal during a $200B/year spending program.
Price is currently well below its 50-day average ($363.12 vs $325.57 close on 2026-07-27) and roughly at its 200-day average ($324.30), i.e. the short-term trend is broken.
what_would_break_thesis: Google Services revenue (the profit engine) declines year-over-year for two consecutive quarters - this would be the first real evidence that AI is eating search.
Google Cloud revenue growth falls below 20% year-over-year for two consecutive quarters while capex stays above $40B per quarter (spending without demand).
Free cash flow is negative for a full fiscal year, or trailing-twelve-month FCF falls below $25B.
Consolidated operating margin falls below 25% for two consecutive quarters (currently 34%).
Company gross margin falls below 50% for two consecutive quarters (currently ~60%).
ROIC falls below 15% on a trailing basis for a full fiscal year.
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 1.5x, i.e. the net cash position is fully spent and Alphabet becomes meaningfully levered to fund capex.
A final, non-appealable antitrust remedy that forces divestiture of Search, Android, YouTube, or the ad-tech stack, or that bans default-search-placement payments.
A material accounting restatement, or a large write-down of the non-marketable equity portfolio that reveals aggressive prior marks.
Total revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive fiscal years.
catalysts: Q3 2026 results (expected late October 2026): evidence that Cloud growth and backlog conversion justify the raised capex, or evidence that they do not.
Capex guidance stabilising or falling in FY2027, which would let free cash flow recover sharply from the depressed $53.3B TTM level.
Clear monetisation of Gemini across Search and Workspace (Gemini App reported at 950M monthly active users) showing up as revenue rather than cost.
Resolution of the US antitrust remedies phase, removing an overhang.
A price pullback toward or below the $237 low end of our fair-value band, which would open a real margin of safety.
